summary: The thesis proposes "Youth Information Entropy" that sums the entropy of surprise, positivity and grammatical fluency. Probabilities estimated using a Japanese BERT model were validated against preference scores from Llama-3-ELYZA-JP-8B, showing a weak but significant positive correlation (r=0.333, p=0.035) across 36 sentences. While long texts and concept diversity remain challenges, it demonstrates the usefulness of integrating surprise and emotion via information theory.
